Anatomical variants · on the lesion side

Level
ASPECTS levelCT score, shown here on MRI

Swipe for coronal and sagittal →

ASPECTS is scored on non-contrast CT; this page shows its regions on an MRI template. It divides the MCA territory into ten regions on two axial levels: at the basal ganglia the caudate head (C), lentiform nucleus (L), internal capsule (IC, only genu and posterior limb), insular ribbon (I) and the cortex M1–M3; at the level of the lateral ventricles above them M4–M6. One point is subtracted for each region with early ischaemic change; 10 is normal. The score applies to ICA and MCA strokes, not to the ACA or the posterior circulation. Dependence and death rise sharply at 7 or less; for thrombectomy within 6 hours, 6 or more stands for a small-to-moderate core. On DWI the score differed from CT by no more than 2 points in one series. The regions are derived from the anatomical atlas of the same toolkit and divided geometrically, so their borders are approximate. Regions that lie at least one third in the occluded territory are marked in amber.

The territories are a population map built from the DWI lesions of 1,298 stroke patients. In an individual patient a territory can be larger or smaller, especially at the borders between territories.

What’s new
  • 0.9.49 · Get it on your device points to the website; the ASPECTS help text is clearer; unused code removed. No change to texts on the cards or to the maps.

Territory map: Digital 3D Brain MRI Arterial Territories Atlas (Liu et al., Johns Hopkins University), CC BY-SA 4.0. Anatomy: the JHU single-subject b0 template shipped with the atlas authors' stroke segmentation toolkit (GPL-3.0). The atlas is a population map built from the DWI lesions of 1,298 patients with acute stroke, so it shows where each territory usually lies; individual territories vary, most at the borders. Small perforator territories (medial lenticulostriate, anterior thalamoperforators) rest mainly on prior anatomical knowledge, because few patients had isolated lesions there. Territories marked “derived” are subdivisions made for this page from the atlas labels. The atlas simplifies boundaries, partly as straight lines; real boundaries vary between individuals. The atlas divides thalamus, midbrain and pons by horizontal planes that lie 6–10 mm too low on this template; here these borders follow the template’s landmarks: pons up to the top of the fourth ventricle (z −43), midbrain up to below the third ventricle (z −27). Slice positions are millimetres in the atlas template, not MNI coordinates. ASPECTS regions are derived for this page from the lobe atlas shipped with the same toolkit (GPL-3.0) and divided geometrically; the insular region is the insular ribbon only, without the claustrum and extreme capsule. Because CC BY-SA 4.0 material may be used in GPL-3.0 works, this page as a whole is offered under GPL-3.0.

Educational model. Real territories vary between people and with collateral flow. Not for clinical decisions.

References

    Every statement on the cards is traced to these references with page numbers; the sources for each card are documented and available on request. Frequencies come from the published series named on the card. Statements that could not be traced to a source were removed.

    How to use

    1. Pick an artery. Tap a vessel on the Circle of Willis or one of the buttons below it. Its territory lights up on the MRI. Border zones have their own buttons.
    2. Set the side. Use Lesion side (left = language-dominant). Deficits switch to right or left automatically.
    3. Explore the MRI. Drag the sliders or scroll on a scan to move through slices. Level jumps to standard levels. Tap any point to line up all three planes and see which artery supplies it; with a mouse, just point at it. Crosshair (under Show) hides or shows the lines.
    4. Read the syndrome. The panel on the right lists the territory, expected deficits (contra = opposite side, ipsi = same side) and a clinical pearl. Where a large published series exists, it shows how often each sign occurred. All references are listed under References at the bottom of the page.
    5. Try variants. Fetal PCA and a hypoplastic A1 change which territory is lost.
    6. Variable borders. The button under Show, next to Level, draws the borders between territories as a hatched band, a reminder that they shift from one person to the next.
    7. ASPECTS. The ASPECTS button under Show draws the ten ASPECTS regions on the two axial levels where they are scored; switch levels in the bar above the scans. ASPECTS is a CT score, shown here on the MRI template. For ICA and MCA occlusions, regions in the territory turn amber and the card shows the score on this map.
    8. Practise. Localize a case shows the findings of a patient; answer by tapping the artery on the angiogram, a vessel button or the territory on the scans. Reveal answer shows the solution, and the score counts along. From findings works the other way: pick the findings, or start from a classic syndrome, and up to five occlusion sites are ranked by a match score (0–100). It shows how well the pattern fits, not how likely the diagnosis is.
    9. Share. Copy link to this view at the bottom of the panel opens exactly this artery, side and variant.

    All territories shows the full colour map. On a phone, swipe sideways for the coronal and sagittal views. Territory boundaries vary between patients. For teaching only, not for clinical decisions.

    Get it on your device

    Nothing to install. The tool runs in any current browser.

    https://senolapaydin.github.io/stroke-explorer/
    iPhone / iPad
    Open the link in Safari. Tap ⋯ next to the address bar → Share → Add to Home Screen → Add. On older iOS versions, tap the Share icon directly.
    Android
    Open the link in Chrome. Tap ⋮ at the top right → Add to Home screen → Add.
    Desktop
    Open the link in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox and bookmark it (Ctrl+D / ⌘D). For offline use, save the page (Ctrl+S / ⌘S) and open the file with a double-click.

    The link needs an internet connection and always shows the latest version. A saved HTML file works offline but stays at its version. The home-screen icon is a shortcut to the link.
